question: A male nurse with a thick beard is caring for a patient with TB. What should he do?

options.A: Shave his beard so the N95 can seal properly
options.B: Wear an N95 right over his beard
options.C: Wear a standard surgical mask instead
options.D: Double-mask with two surgical masks

question: Why do pregnant women need to eat plenty of dark green leafy vegetables?

options.C: They replace the need for all routine prenatal vitamin supplements
options.D: They prevent the mother from gaining any excess weight during the pregnancy

question: Which of these habits helps keep oral syringes clean and free of germs?

question: What is the main focus of a maternity home in the community?

options.A: Managing low-risk pregnancies and normal deliveries

options.D: Providing long-term pediatric intensive care

question: Which of these is NOT a typical challenge for monitoring and evaluation in resource-limited settings?

options.A: Inconsistent electricity and poor internet connectivity
options.B: Staff shortages and heavy workloads for nurses

question: When a community nurse teaches local mothers about healthy weaning foods for babies, what role is she playing?

options.A: Pharmacist

question: Why is a mother's nutrition directly linked to her baby's health?

options.A: Nutritional deficiencies only affect the mother's hair and skin
options.B: Poor maternal nutrition often results in low birth weight and developmental challenges
options.C: Infants do not depend on maternal nutrient stores during pregnancy
options.D: A mother's diet has no effect on the fetus once the placenta forms

question: You are working in a busy ward where running water has temporarily stopped. What is the best way to keep up with infection control?

options.A: Wear the same pair of gloves for all patients to save supplies
options.B: Use stored clean water and alcohol rubs correctly between patients
options.C: Skip hand hygiene until running water is restored to the clinic
options.D: Reuse single-use syringes after rinsing them in warm water

explanation: Brilliant problem-solving! Using safe stored water and alcohol rubs keeps your hands clean and keeps your patients safe even when the plumbing acts up. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T1#GNS122_U2_T1_h7)

question: Why do we ask a patient to close their eyes during a sensory nerve physical examination?

options.A: To relax the autonomic nervous system and lower blood pressure
options.B: To prevent accidental corneal injury from reflex movements
options.C: To prevent visual compensation and ensure accurate sensory testing
options.D: To enhance the patient's hearing during verbal instructions

question: Which antenatal care service is most crucial for pregnant teenagers?

options.A: Intensive nutritional counseling and iron supplementation
options.B: Mandatory enrollment in adult literacy classes
options.C: Immediate scheduling of elective tubal ligation
options.D: Restriction of physical activity throughout all trimesters

explanation: Because teen moms are still growing and easily get anemic, good nutrition guidance and iron supplements are absolute top priorities. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T6#GNS225_U6_T6_h7)

question: Why does the formal healthcare system train Traditional Birth Attendants (TBAs)?

options.A: Licensing them to perform major surgical operations independently
options.B: Replacing all professional midwives in urban hospitals
options.C: Employing them as permanent government administrative officers
options.D: Teaching them to recognize danger signs and refer complicated labor early

explanation: Exactly right! Since many mothers still visit TBAs, training them to spot danger signs early helps save lives by getting women to the hospital fast when trouble arises. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T5#GNS124_U2_T5_h5)

question: A patient with painful second-degree burns on both feet is admitted to your ward. Which bed accessory is a must-have for their comfort?

options.A: An air ring
options.B: A bed cradle
options.C: A bed block
options.D: A footboard

explanation: You got it! Burned skin cannot handle the heavy weight and friction of standard bedsheets, so a bed cradle is a lifesaver for pain relief and healing. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T4#GNS112_U4_T4_h3)

question: Which joint is most famously affected during a first-time gout attack?

options.A: The acromioclavicular joint of the shoulder
options.B: The proximal interphalangeal joint of the index finger
options.C: The metatarsophalangeal joint of the big toe
options.D: The temporomandibular joint of the jaw

explanation: Classic nursing knowledge! The big toe joint (known clinically as the metatarsophalangeal joint) is the absolute favorite spot for a first gout flare. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T15#GNS222_U1_T15_h3)

question: What does 'primary hypertension' mean?

options.A: High blood pressure with no single identifiable medical cause
options.B: Blood pressure that only affects young children and infants
options.C: High blood pressure caused by a single known kidney disease
options.D: A temporary spike in pressure caused by severe acute stress

explanation: Exactly! Primary (or essential) hypertension develops gradually over time without one specific underlying medical trigger. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T2#GNS313_U3_T2_h2)

question: Why do nurse researchers rely so much on a theoretical framework?

options.A: It connects abstract nursing ideas directly to concrete patient care
options.B: It replaces the literature review section of the proposal
options.C: It guarantees that the research will be published in a journal
options.D: It eliminates the need for statistical data analysis entirely

explanation: Nursing is all about practice! Frameworks help us bridge the gap between big academic ideas and the real-world care we give patients every day. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T12#GNS217_U3_T12_h1)

question: Why should you sort waste right at the bedside or where it is generated?

options.A: To speed up the physical transport of bins to the incinerator
options.B: To prevent hazardous waste from contaminating general trash
options.C: To reduce the number of waste bins needed in each ward
options.D: To make it easier for patients to clean up their bedside

explanation: Sorting waste immediately stops dangerous items from mixing with safe rubbish. It keeps disposal safe and easy for everyone! [learn more](GST114_U6_T8#GST114_U6_T8_h3)

question: Why must nurse managers actively supervise instead of just writing policies on paper?

options.A: Written policies alone cannot guarantee staff will follow them safely
options.B: Nurse managers have no other administrative duties assigned to them
options.C: Staff nurses prefer having constant supervision during every shift
options.D: Hospital accreditation bodies legally require daily verbal check-ins

explanation: Having a policy on paper is a good start, but checking actual practice ensures everyone is safe and rules are followed in real clinical situations. [learn more](GST321_U1_T19#GST321_U1_T19_h1)

question: On the standard muscle strength scale, what grade means complete paralysis with zero movement?

options.A: Grade 5
options.B: Grade 0
options.C: Grade 3
options.D: Grade 1

explanation: Grade 0 means absolute zero movement, while Grade 5 is strong, normal muscle power. You've got this! [learn more](GNS222_U3_T4#GNS222_U3_T4_h4)

question: When taking a baseline reproductive health history, what should you include?

options.A: Childhood vaccination records
options.B: Daily dietary calorie and sodium intake
options.C: Menstrual patterns and obstetric history
options.D: Family history of cardiovascular disease only

explanation: Great job! A good reproductive history focuses on menstrual cycles, past pregnancies, and sexual health to understand the patient's baseline. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T14#GNS311_U1_T14_h2)

question: Which of these is a major direct cause of maternal mortality in Nigeria?

options.A: Severe bleeding after childbirth
options.B: Untreated childhood measles
options.C: Chronic adult asthma
options.D: Seasonal malaria outbreaks in men

explanation: Severe bleeding after delivery (known as postpartum hemorrhage) is one of the leading direct causes of maternal death. As a future nurse, knowing this helps you spot why rapid postpartum care is so vital. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T4#GNS216_U1_T4_h2)

question: Why does a woman sometimes notice light spotting right before her period starts?

options.A: A sudden drop in hormone levels causes the uterine lining to start breaking down.
options.B: The corpus luteum grows too large and presses against the uterine wall.
options.C: An excessive surge of follicle-stimulating hormone forces blood vessels to leak.
options.D: High levels of progesterone cause the cervix to dilate prematurely.

explanation: When estrogen and progesterone take a sudden dip, the uterine lining loses its support, leading to that little bit of early spotting. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T5#GNS121_U5_T5_h4)

question: Why is gender-based violence classified as a public health issue rather than just a private matter?

options.A: Because health insurance companies fully cover all related legal fees
options.B: Because it causes widespread physical and mental harm that impacts community wellbeing
options.C: Because hospitals are legally required to arrest perpetrators on sight
options.D: Because it only occurs inside public government buildings

explanation: The extensive physical injuries and psychological trauma resulting from abuse place a massive burden on healthcare systems and society. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T12#GNS312_U4_T12_h1)

question: Where is compact bone tissue found in the highest amounts?

options.A: Inside the ends of short bones
options.B: Surrounding the bone marrow cavity loosely
options.C: In the shafts of long bones
options.D: Within the center of flat skull bones

explanation: The shafts of long bones need thick compact bone to bear body weight and resist bending forces. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T2#GNS121_U3_T2_h1)

question: What is the medical term for the yellowing of the skin and eyes caused by the rapid breakdown of red blood cells?

options.A: Cyanosis
options.B: Jaundice
options.C: Pallor
options.D: Erythema

explanation: Jaundice happens when red blood cells break down quickly, releasing excess bilirubin which the liver processes more slowly than it is produced. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h3)

question: Why is it dangerous to leave jewelry on a patient when sending the body to the mortuary?

options.A: It makes the body bag too heavy to lift safely
options.B: It violates the medical license of the attending physician
options.C: It interferes with the natural cooling process of the body
options.D: It increases the risk of loss and creates unnecessary conflict

explanation: Unsecured valuables often go missing during body transfers, leading to serious accusations and distress for the family. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T10#GNS221_U4_T10_h5)

question: What is a very common result of high humidity inside an oxygen tent?

options.A: Water condensation building up on the inner plastic walls
options.B: Sudden dropping of the room's overall humidity level
options.C: Freezing of the oxygen gas into solid ice crystals
options.D: Complete drying out of the patient's nasal passages

question: At what point in the procedure should you release the tourniquet?

options.A: Immediately after the first blood tube is filled
options.B: Before pulling the needle out of the vein
options.C: Before inserting the needle into the skin
options.D: After applying the adhesive bandage to the arm

explanation: Remember to release the tourniquet before taking the needle out. This stops extra blood from leaking out and prevents a nasty bruise from forming. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T8#GNS122_U1_T8_h6)

question: Why is it sometimes a bad idea to immediately stop infectious diarrhoea with medicine?

options.A: It permanently destroys the muscles of the colon
options.B: It completely stops the absorption of all vitamins
options.C: It traps harmful toxins and bacteria inside the gut
options.D: It causes an immediate spike in blood pressure

explanation: When germs cause diarrhoea, your body tries to flush them out. Stopping the flow too soon just keeps the bad stuff trapped inside you! [learn more](GNS223_U3_T3#GNS223_U3_T3_h1)

question: What happens right away during the emission phase?

options.A: Urine is forced out of the kidneys
options.B: Semen gathers in the prostatic urethra
options.C: The external sphincter permanently relaxes
options.D: Sperm are newly created in the bladder

explanation: Emission is just the gathering step—sperm and fluids team up and wait in the upper urethra before the big push outward! [learn more](GNS121_U4_T5#GNS121_U4_T5_h3)

question: A patient comes back two days after an abscess drainage with a fever and redness that is spreading outward from the wound. What does this mean?

options.A: Worsening infection requiring prompt medical reassessment
options.B: An allergic reaction to the cotton inside the dressing
options.C: Successful eradication of all bacteria from the body
options.D: Normal healing response as the deep tissues close

explanation: Spreading redness and fever are warning signs that the infection is fighting back and traveling further. The patient needs a doctor to take a look right away. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T4#GNS311_U4_T4_h5)

question: Why is family planning counseling so important before a mother is discharged from the postpartum ward?

options.A: Ovulation can occur before the first postpartum menstrual period returns
options.B: Sexual intercourse is strictly forbidden for a full year
options.C: Hormonal contraceptives are required to stop lochia flow
options.D: Pregnancy is impossible during the first six months postpartum

question: When an epidemiologist asks where and when a disease is happening, which component are they studying?

options.A: Prognosis
options.B: Distribution
options.C: Diagnosis
options.D: Determinants

explanation: Great try! 'Distribution' is all about mapping out the frequency and pattern of health events—looking at time, place, and who is affected. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T1#GNS313_U1_T1_h2)

question: Why is Crew Resource Management (CRM) so helpful for flight nurses?

options.A: It replaces the need for medical equipment maintenance

options.C: It ensures pilots make all medical decisions alone

question: A nurse sees that the clinic's reported vaccinations are way higher than the empty vaccine vials thrown away. What should she suspect?

options.C: Proper functioning of the vaccine refrigerator

question: A patient comes in with a suspected blood clot in their leg vein (deep vein thrombosis). What scan will the doctor likely order?

options.A: Renal B-Mode ultrasound
options.B: Pelvic M-Mode ultrasound
options.C: Cardiac echocardiogram
options.D: Vascular Doppler ultrasound

question: Which two blood tests do doctors frequently order to check for general inflammation in the body?

options.A: Sodium and potassium
options.B: Hemoglobin and hematocrit
options.C: ESR and CRP
options.D: BUN and creatinine

explanation: ESR (Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate) and CRP (C-Reactive Protein) are your go-to blood markers for spotting inflammation anywhere in the body. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T11#GNS222_U1_T11_h5)

question: Where do endocrine glands release their hormones directly?

options.B: The lymphatic vessels only

options.D: The bloodstream

question: In newly arrived displaced populations, which health issues are most commonly reported?

options.A: Diarrheal diseases and acute respiratory infections
options.B: Complications from elective cosmetic surgeries
options.C: Chronic sports injuries from professional training
options.D: Rare genetic disorders requiring gene therapy

question: What is a very common and easily fixed cause of muscle spasms during pregnancy?

options.A: High protein intake
options.B: Excess water
options.C: Low fiber intake
options.D: Dehydration

question: Roughly what percentage of patients with full Korsakoff syndrome make a complete recovery?

options.D: About 20 percent

question: Why are stool softeners frequently given to patients recovering from major surgery?

question: What is the primary underlying cause of inherited degenerative disorders?

options.A: Vitamin and mineral deficiencies
options.B: Acute physical trauma to the brain
options.C: Genetic mutations in the DNA

question: Which symptom pattern is most typical for someone with Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS)?

options.A: Severe sudden constipation that leads straight to a bowel blockage

question: How do Hepatitis B and C viruses primarily cause damage inside the human body?

question: What document lets a competent person state their medical treatment preferences before they lose the ability to decide?

options.A: Standard hospital admission form

options.C: Incident liability report
options.D: Advance directive or living will

explanation: Correct! An advance directive gives people a voice in their future medical care even if they later become unable to speak for themselves. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T5#GNS324_U2_T5_h6)

question: A surgical instrument slips from your hand and lands partially on the edge of the instrument table tray. What should you do?

options.C: Inspect the instrument to see if it touched the floor.

question: Which of these options is NOT a secondary sexual characteristic?

question: What emotional need is especially important for elderly family members?

options.A: Trying to fit in with teenage trends
options.B: Feeling respected and protected from loneliness
options.C: Wanting zero help from anyone at all
options.D: Living in high-stress, competitive environments

explanation: As people age and face physical changes, knowing they are valued, respected, and not forgotten keeps their spirits high and emotional health intact. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T6#GNS314_U1_T6_h3)

question: What is a primary responsibility of a community health nurse in preventing infectious diseases?

options.A: Manufacturing sterile surgical instruments in the clinic kitchen
options.B: Isolating entire towns when a single flu case is reported
options.C: Educating families on hygiene, sanitation, and vaccination

explanation: Community nurses empower everyday people with the practical knowledge needed to stop infections at home. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T95#GNS214_U1_T95_h8)

question: Which of these is a very common fall hazard found in many homes?

options.A: Loose scatter rugs on polished floors
options.B: Low furniture located near the walls
options.C: Hardwood floors without any coverings
options.D: Bright lighting in the hallway stairs

question: What is the main difference between a clinical leader and a clinical manager?

options.A: Leaders focus on inspiring people and driving change, while managers focus on operational systems and stability.
options.B: Leaders handle the payroll and disciplinary actions, while managers take care of patient assessments.
options.C: Leaders rely purely on formal authority, while managers rely solely on personal charisma.
options.D: Leaders work exclusively in outpatient clinics, while managers work only in intensive care units.

explanation: You've got it! Think of managers as keeping the ship running smoothly day-to-day, and leaders as steering the ship toward new horizons. [learn more](GST321_U3_T1#GST321_U3_T1_h2)

question: Which part of the brain acts as the body's internal thermostat?

options.A: Hypothalamus
options.B: Cerebellum

question: When doing a thoracentesis, where should the needle enter the chest to keep blood vessels and nerves safe?

question: What is the medical term for the natural loss of muscle mass and strength as people age?

options.A: The rapid calcification of heart valves in older adults
options.B: The abnormal softening of bones due to vitamin deficiency
options.C: The sudden inflammation of fluid-filled joint sacs

question: About how long is the duodenum in an adult human?

options.B: Ten centimeters
options.C: One hundred centimeters
options.D: Twenty-five centimeters

question: Your patient has chest congestion with thick mucus that just won't budge. What drug class should you expect the doctor to order?

options.A: A topical anesthetic

options.D: A loop diuretic

question: Why do nurses commonly use compresses in the ward?

options.C: To permanently cure chronic autoimmune joint diseases
options.D: To provide localized pain relief and reduce inflammation

question: Why is a chest X-ray routinely ordered after a thoracocentesis?

options.A: To check if any skin sutures need to be removed immediately

question: What actually happens during the 'promotion' stage of cancer development?

options.B: Cancer cells immediately travel to the brain
options.C: All abnormal cells safely destroy themselves
options.D: Normal DNA is completely repaired by enzymes

question: What is the best position for a patient who needs help with eating?

options.A: Flat on the back with neck extended

question: What should an auxiliary nurse do if asked to perform a procedure they have never been taught?

question: What is the very first thing a nurse must do if a patient reacts badly to an IV medication?

question: When should the nurse verify the placement of a nasogastric tube?

question: You advise a recovering patient to make half their plate colorful fruits and veggies. Which food group are you focusing on?

question: What should a nurse do if a sound-minded patient at home refuses treatment?

question: What receptor combination is the trademark of second-generation (atypical) antipsychotics?

question: What is the main job of the skin when acting as a sense organ?

question: Which mental health condition is frequently missed in older adults because it often hides behind physical complaints like body aches?

question: Why do you need to be extra careful with cleaning liquids on a smart bed?

question: When would you expect to see bladder irrigation actually ordered for a patient?

question: A family'breadwinner' sustains a permanent physical injury and loses their job. What is the most likely outcome for the household?

question: What is the primary purpose of an adult day care home?

question: Which of the following is an effective strategy for reducing household expenditure on proteins without sacrificing nutrition?

question: Which check is considered the ultimate gold standard to confirm your autoclave cycle actually worked?

question: When must a nurse choose soap and water over an alcohol-based hand rub?

question: How can a nurse test the motor strength of the Trigeminal nerve (CN V)?

question: What is a major downside of fiscal decentralization in the Nigerian health sector?

question: What neurotransmitter is released by all preganglionic neurons in both the sympathetic and parasympathetic systems?

question: What is the main way that antiemetic (anti-nausea) drugs stop vomiting?

question: A nurse checks lab results for an older adult on a new drug and sees that serum creatinine levels are rising. What does this usually mean?

question: Which piece of information is most critical to document immediately during a patient's admission assessment?

question: What is the number one thing that encourages young people to open up and share sensitive health info with a nurse?

question: A village school lacks a clean water supply, putting children at risk of waterborne diseases. What is the best community-driven action to take?

question: A young female patient has lower abdominal pain and cries out in severe pain when the nurse moves her cervix during a pelvic exam. What is the most likely condition?

options.A: Uterine fibroids
options.B: Primary dysmenorrhea
options.C: Polycystic Ovary Syndrome
options.D: Pelvic Inflammatory Disease

explanation: That intense pain when moving the cervix is called 'cervical motion tenderness' (or a positive chandelier sign), and it's a classic red flag for PID. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T10#GNS311_U1_T10_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT one of the classic local signs of acute inflammation?

options.A: Pain
options.B: Swelling
options.C: Numbness
options.D: Redness

explanation: Remember the classic signs: redness, heat, swelling, pain, and loss of function. Numbness points more toward a nerve issue than simple inflammation! [learn more](GNS123_U1_T1#GNS123_U1_T1_h4)

question: Why is the variable region of an antibody so important?

options.A: It allows the body to recognize many different antigens
options.B: It provides the structural strength to hold the Y shape
options.C: It helps the antibody attach to normal red blood cells
options.D: It dissolves the cell wall of invading bacteria directly

explanation: Because our bodies face countless different germs, the variable region acts like a shape-shifter at the tips of the antibody, creating diverse binding sites to lock onto various invaders. [learn more](GST114_U4_T3#GST114_U4_T3_h2)

question: What actually happens during DOTS (Directly Observed Therapy) for a TB patient?

options.A: A health worker watches the patient swallow every dose
options.B: Blood tests are run daily to measure drug levels in the serum
options.C: The patient reports their pill intake via phone once a week
options.D: Family members check the pill bottles at the end of each month

explanation: Under DOTS, a healthcare worker physically watches the patient take their meds to ensure they finish the whole course without missing days. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T6#GNS223_U2_T6_h4)

question: Under the WHO medical rules, what does a Category 4 classification mean for a contraceptive method?

options.A: The benefits outweigh the risks in most cases
options.B: There are no restrictions on using the method
options.C: The method can be used with routine monitoring
options.D: The method represents an unacceptable health risk

explanation: Category 4 means 'Stop!' — the condition is too dangerous, and the contraceptive must not be used because it puts the client's health at serious risk. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T013#GNS226_U6_T013_h3)

question: What is a major, life-altering complication frequently linked to advanced endometriosis?

options.A: Chronic kidney failure
options.B: Infertility
options.C: Gestational diabetes
options.D: Systemic hypertension

explanation: Due to scarring and ongoing inflammation, getting pregnant can become a real hurdle for many women battling advanced endometriosis. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T21#GNS216_U5_T21_h9)

question: When should the nurse label the collected blood specimen tube?

options.A: At the bedside immediately after the blood draw
options.B: Inside the laboratory before handing it to the technician
options.C: At the nursing station after finishing all morning rounds
options.D: Before entering the patient room to save time

explanation: Labeling specimens at the bedside immediately after collection ensures proper patient identification and prevents mislabeling errors. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T12#GNS221_U2_T12_h5)

question: Where is the hypodermis located in relation to the main skin layers?

options.A: Below the dermis
options.B: Above the epidermis
options.C: Between the epidermis and dermis
options.D: Inside the blood vessels

explanation: The hypodermis lies directly beneath the dermis to anchor the skin to underlying tissues. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T5#GNS211_U2_T5_h1)

question: Why do steroid hormones need carrier proteins to travel through the blood?

options.A: Because carrier proteins protect them from being digested by blood enzymes
options.B: Because they are fat-soluble and do not dissolve well in water-based blood plasma
options.C: Because they are too large to fit through the walls of blood capillaries alone
options.D: Because carrier proteins are required to activate their chemical structure

explanation: Since blood is mostly water and steroid hormones are fat-based, they don't mix well on their own. Carrier proteins act like VIP transport vehicles to get them safely through the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T3#GNS211_U1_T3_h2)

question: Which group forms the backbone of direct healthcare delivery in Nigerian primary clinics?

options.A: International policy makers
options.B: Hospital accountants
options.C: Nurses and midwives
options.D: Pharmaceutical manufacturers

explanation: That's you! Nurses and midwives provide the vast majority of direct maternal and child health care across our communities. You are truly the heartbeat of healthcare delivery. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T4#GNS216_U1_T4_h8)

question: Why do patients use a spacer with a metered-dose inhaler?

options.A: To increase the total dose of medication delivered to the stomach
options.B: To measure the exact volume of air the patient breathes out
options.C: To slow down the spray and trap large particles so more drug reaches the lungs
options.D: To convert liquid medication into an aerosol mist using oxygen

explanation: Without a spacer, the medicine often just hits the back of the throat. The spacer slows down the spray so the drug can float gently and deeply into the lungs where it's needed. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T2#GNS223_U2_T2_h5)

question: Which sign is a classic clue that someone has hyperthyroidism?

options.A: SlOWed heart rate and sluggish mentation
options.B: Intolerance to cold room temperatures
options.C: Severe constipation and dry coarse skin
options.D: Weight loss despite an increased appetite

explanation: Hyperthyroidism puts the body's engine into overdrive! Patients burn through calories so fast that they lose weight even though they are eating way more food than usual. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T14#GNS222_U2_T14_h3)

question: Which of the following is an absolute contraindication for rectal medication administration?

options.A: Mild high blood pressure
options.B: Mild headache and body fatigue
options.C: History of seasonal allergies
options.D: Recent rectal or bowel surgery

explanation: Inserting a suppository into a healing surgical site can damage tissue, cause pain, and disrupt sutures. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T18#GNS125_U3_T18_h6)

question: Which payment setup best promotes true equity in a health system?

options.A: Progressive prepayment systems where wealthier individuals contribute more to fund care for everyone
options.B: Relying entirely on patient donations collected inside hospital waiting rooms
options.C: Strict out-of-pocket user fees charged at the hospital door for every single service
options.D: Flat-rate private insurance premiums that cost the same for low- and high-income earners

explanation: When those who earn more chip in a bit extra, it helps protect and cover those who have less. That's true fairness! [learn more](GST322_U4_T6#GST322_U4_T6_h5)

question: Which symptom is a classic sign of orthostatic hypotension when a patient stands up suddenly?

options.A: Dizziness or lightheadedness
options.B: Sudden severe chest pain
options.C: Uncontrollable muscle tremors
options.D: Rapid elevation of body temperature

explanation: When blood pressure drops fast upon standing, the brain momentarily misses out on optimal blood flow, making the patient feel dizzy or lightheaded. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T6#GNS111_U2_T6_h6)

question: Which of the following will NOT typically cause prevalence to increase?

options.A: An increase in new infections
options.B: A long duration of the illness
options.C: Migration of sick people into the town
options.D: A high death rate from the disease

explanation: A high mortality rate removes people from the population quickly, which lowers prevalence rather than raising it. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T12#GNS313_U1_T12_h4)

question: What makes controlling Sexually Transmitted Infections (STIs) so tricky in communities?

options.A: STIs cannot be transmitted if the infected person takes vitamins
options.B: Laboratory tests are completely unavailable in most health clinics
options.C: Many infections present with mild or silent symptoms
options.D: Antibiotics can cure viral infections just as easily as bacterial ones

explanation: Many STIs show zero signs at first! People feel totally fine, so they unknowingly spread the infection before realizing they need treatment. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T3#GNS216_U1_T3_h4)

question: What is the very first practical safety step before applying a prepared warm poultice to a patient?

options.A: Wrap the entire body in thick blankets
options.B: Test the temperature of the mixture
options.C: Leave the room for thirty minutes
options.D: Scrub the skin hard with stiff wire wool

explanation: Always test the temperature to prevent accidental burns before the substance touches the patient's skin. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T10#GNS221_U3_T10_h6)

question: How does keeping a community clean actually help family finances?

options.A: Governments no longer need to collect any domestic taxes
options.B: Families spend less money on medications for preventable illnesses
options.C: Agricultural crop prices drop instantly in local markets
options.D: Hospitals can close down completely due to a lack of patients

explanation: Exactly! When people stay healthy, families save the money they would have spent treating repeated infections. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T9#GNS112_U5_T9_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT used to measure the quality of a nursing unit?

options.A: Patient fall rates and hospital-acquired infections
options.B: Medication error tracking and incident reports
options.C: Patient satisfaction survey scores
options.D: The favorite holiday destination of the nursing staff

explanation: You nailed it! Quality care is measured by safety outcomes and patient happiness, not personal staff trivia. [learn more](GST321_U6_T1#GST321_U6_T1_h7)

question: A patient is physically stable after recovering from an intentional overdose. What is the most important next step in their care?

options.A: Discharge the patient immediately with a warning never to return
options.B: Scold the patient for wasting hospital resources and staff time
options.C: Arrange for a mental health evaluation and ongoing psychological support
options.D: Assume the underlying issue is resolved and stop all observation

explanation: Physical healing is only half the battle. For intentional self-harm, a psychiatric assessment and emotional support before discharge are essential for keeping the patient safe. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T7#GNS215_U5_T7_h7)

question: Which of these is considered an environmental barrier to good communication?

options.A: Loud monitor alarms and constant hallway interruptions
options.B: A language difference between nurse and patient
options.C: A patient's severe hearing impairment or old age
options.D: Deep personal anxiety about an upcoming surgery

explanation: Yes! Noise and lack of privacy in the ward are classic environmental hurdles that make talking difficult. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T2#GNS112_U3_T2_h5)

question: What approach matters most when doing a physical assessment on an FGM survivor?

options.A: Insisting that family members stay in the room to answer questions
options.B: Avoiding any visual inspection of the perineal area entirely
options.C: Trauma-informed care that prioritizes patient dignity and consent
options.D: Rushing through the examination to minimize patient embarrassment

explanation: Trauma-informed care builds trust, makes the patient feel safe, and respects her boundaries during sensitive exams. You are becoming a wonderfully compassionate nurse! [learn more](GNS312_U1_T2#GNS312_U1_T2_h6)

question: Which sign strongly suggests a pregnant woman's uterus has ruptured during a difficult labor?

options.A: A gradual increase in contractions with steady pink show
options.B: Sudden sharp tearing pain and disappearance of contractions
options.C: High fever accompanied by foul-smelling vaginal discharge
options.D: Mild lower backache that improves when walking around

explanation: If contractions suddenly stop after a sharp, tearing pain, think uterine rupture. It's a major emergency! [learn more](GNS225_U3_T12#GNS225_U3_T12_h6)

question: During a laryngoscopy, a patient's oxygen level suddenly drops from 98% to 85%. What is your immediate action as the nurse?

options.A: Administer an oral pain medication to relax the vocal cords.
options.B: Document the drop in the chart and wait for the doctor to finish looking.
options.C: Alert the clinician, stop the procedure, and provide supplemental oxygen or bag-valve-mask ventilation.
options.D: Ask the patient to sit up straight and take three deep breaths through their mouth.

explanation: Safety first! A sudden drop in oxygen means you must stop what's happening right away, get help, and give the patient oxygen. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T4#GNS221_U2_T4_h6)

question: Why must thiamine always be given BEFORE glucose to a deficient patient?

options.A: Glucose burns up the remaining thiamine and can worsen brain injury
options.B: Glucose stops the body from absorbing any vitamins
options.C: Thiamine stops glucose from causing an allergic reaction
options.D: Glucose mixes with the vitamin and makes it poisonous

explanation: Exactly! Giving sugar without thiamine forces starving cells to work, using up their last bits of vitamin and causing rapid brain damage. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T7#GNS222_U4_T7_h5)

question: How can a nurse avoid getting 'tunnel vision' when a medical emergency happens?

options.A: Refusing to speak to any colleagues who enter the emergency room
options.B: Leaving the ward entirely to complete paperwork in a quiet office
options.C: Pausing briefly to scan the broader situation and ensure other patients are safe
options.D: Focusing exclusively on a single piece of equipment until the shift ends

explanation: Take a mental step back! Pausing for just a few seconds helps you keep the big picture in mind so nothing else goes wrong on the ward. [learn more](GST321_U4_T4#GST321_U4_T4_h6)

question: A patient arrives at the clinic pale, dizzy, with a fast pulse and severe tummy pain after an unsafe abortion. What is your immediate nursing priority?

options.A: Send the patient home with instructions to return next week
options.B: Begin lengthy administrative registration before any medical action
options.C: Wait for laboratory blood test results before providing any fluids
options.D: Stabilize vital signs, start IV fluids, and prepare for emergency care

explanation: Pale skin, rapid pulse, and dizziness are warning signs of shock and hemorrhage. Your quick action with IV fluids and stabilization can save a life! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T020#GNS226_U5_T020_h5)

question: Why must a nurse know the difference between traditional scarification and self-harm scars?

options.A: To ensure the client is charged the correct hospital fees
options.B: To report the family to the local village chief
options.C: To guide appropriate medical treatment and mental health support
options.D: To decide which type of antibiotic ointment to sell

explanation: Exactly! Understanding where scars come from helps you provide the right physical care and emotional support tailored to your patient. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T7#GNS225_U6_T7_h5)

question: What is the main job of state-level health bodies like HEFAMAA regarding hospitals and clinics?

options.A: Inspecting and accrediting physical hospital buildings and operating environments
options.B: Designing the academic curriculum for newly established medical schools
options.C: Paying the monthly salaries of clinical staff working in private clinics
options.D: Procuring pharmaceutical drugs for government-owned tertiary hospitals

explanation: Agencies like HEFAMAA check hospitals to make sure their buildings are clean, safe, and fit for treating patients. [learn more](GST322_U4_T10#GST322_U4_T10_h2)

question: Why is checking drug compatibility important when administering multiple intravenous infusions?

options.A: Incompatible drugs can react and form solid crystals that block the catheter
options.B: Combining medications changes the colour of the plastic infusion tubing
options.C: Mixing drugs always causes the patient to develop a skin rash
options.D: Incompatible solutions neutralize each other and make nurses look careless

explanation: Chemical reactions between mixed drugs can create precipitates that clog the line and endanger the patient. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T4#GNS122_U1_T4_h6)

question: What is the normal baseline range for a healthy fetal heart rate?

options.A: 60 to 100 beats per minute
options.B: 110 to 160 beats per minute
options.C: 80 to 120 beats per minute
options.D: 140 to 200 beats per minute

explanation: Spot on! An unborn baby's heart beats much faster than an adult's, usually staying comfortably between 110 and 160 bpm. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T4#GNS123_U2_T4_h5)

question: Why is the transformation zone easily prone to irritation?

options.A: It has a very thick layer of hard skin cells that easily trap heat.
options.B: It experiences constant muscular contractions during the menstrual period.
options.C: It features active cell transitions that make it vulnerable to external factors.
options.D: It lacks any protective mucus layer to shield it from normal bacteria.

explanation: Correct! Because cells are actively changing and meeting right there, this zone is extra sensitive to infections and friction. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T16#GNS216_U5_T16_h2)

question: What is the main job of the endocrine system in the body?

options.A: Filtering metabolic waste products out of circulating blood plasma
options.B: Directing immediate, split-second muscle movements and reflexes
options.C: Coordinating slow, sustained processes like growth and metabolism
options.D: Producing physical barriers to protect internal organs from pathogens

explanation: While your nervous system handles quick reflexes (like pulling your hand from a hot stove), the endocrine system takes the long view—slowly and steadily managing things like your growth, mood, and metabolism. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T3#GNS211_U1_T3_h1)

question: Why do physical signs of puberty usually show up long after the internal hormonal changes have already started?

options.A: Because the skin blocks hormones from reaching the rest of the body early on
options.B: Because bones refuse to lengthen until a person turns twelve years old
options.C: Because internal chemical signals must build up and stimulate target organs over time
options.D: Because children eat too many processed foods before growing up

explanation: Well done! Hormones start working quietly behind the scenes in the brain way before you can actually see any physical changes on the outside. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T13#GNS121_U5_T13_h1)

question: Which body language helps build instant trust during a home visit?

options.A: Standing over the patient while writing notes rapidly
options.B: Checking your wristwatch every two minutes
options.C: Crossing your arms tightly across your chest
options.D: Sitting down at eye level with open body language

explanation: Pulling up a chair and sitting at eye level shows the patient that you have time for them, making them feel valued and relaxed. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T3#GNS324_U2_T3_h8)

question: Which nursing advice helps prevent burnout in a gifted child with a packed daily schedule?

options.A: Adding more advanced academic subjects to the day
options.B: Encouraging unstructured play and rest periods
options.C: Increasing pressure to win competitive awards
options.D: Isolating the child from group activities

explanation: Even the brightest minds need a break! Encouraging free play and rest protects them from mental burnout. You've completed this set—awesome job today! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T1#GNS225_U5_T1_h6)

question: Which blood test results shoot up when liver cells are actively inflamed or damaged?

options.A: Red blood cell count and hemoglobin
options.B: Serum sodium and potassium
options.C: Blood urea nitrogen and creatinine
options.D: ALT and AST

explanation: Easy to remember: ALT and AST are special enzymes stored inside liver cells. When those cells get injured, the enzymes leak out into the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T16#GNS313_U2_T16_h5)

question: What is the key difference between skeletal traction and skin traction?

options.A: Skin traction involves surgical insertion of metal wires
options.B: Skeletal traction attaches directly to the bone using pins
options.C: Skin traction uses heavy weights for longer periods
options.D: Skeletal traction only requires adhesive strips on the skin

explanation: You got this! Skeletal traction uses surgically placed pins to pull right on the bone, while skin traction applies the pulling force gently through the soft tissues outside. Great job! [learn more](GNS221_U1_T9#GNS221_U1_T9_h1)

question: A patient is having a severe panic attack, breathing fast, and crying out in fear. What is your best first nursing action?

options.A: Hand the patient a stack of educational pamphlets about panic disorder.
options.B: Stay with the patient and speak in calm, short sentences while guiding their breathing.
options.C: Speak loudly and rapidly to snap the patient out of their panic state.
options.D: Leave the room immediately to give the patient privacy to calm down.

explanation: Wonderful nursing care! Your calm presence and steady, simple guidance help anchor a patient when their world feels like it's crashing down. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T5#GNS314_U2_T5_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a core part of an effective birth preparedness plan?

options.A: Identifying a designated health facility with skilled staff
options.B: Arranging reliable emergency transportation in advance
options.C: Buying expensive decorative clothing for the newborn
options.D: Saving emergency funds for unexpected medical costs

explanation: You got it! Fancy baby clothes are nice, but true emergency readiness focuses on transport, money, and skilled hands to help deliver safely. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T009#GNS226_U2_T009_h7)

question: Why do patients often forget to mention herbs and local remedies during a drug history?

options.A: These substances dissolve completely in the body within minutes
options.B: Doctors automatically know every herb sold in local markets
options.C: They view them as food or lifestyle items, not real drugs
options.D: Federal law prohibits patients from discussing herbs in hospitals

explanation: Patients view everyday teas and herbal mixtures as harmless, so they don't think to mention them. Asking probing questions bridges this gap! [learn more](GNS215_U2_T2#GNS215_U2_T2_h5)

question: Why are elderly patients much more sensitive to side effects when taking multiple drugs?

options.A: They refuse to take any form of liquid medication or syrup.
options.B: Their immune systems reject synthetic chemical compounds instantly.
options.C: They always forget to take their medications at the correct hour.
options.D: Their bodies process and clear drugs more slowly due to aging organs.

explanation: As organs age, the liver and kidneys don't clear drugs as fast. This causes medications to hang around longer and build up in the body. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T9#GNS215_U1_T9_h3)

question: Your clinical tutor watches you clean a wound, points out a mistake, and shows you the right way right there. What kind of evaluation is this?

options.A: Norm-referenced
options.B: Formative
options.C: Financial
options.D: Summative

explanation: Spot-on! Catching a mistake and correcting it on the spot to help you learn is a classic formative assessment. [learn more](GST321_U9_T2#GST321_U9_T2_h3)

question: A nursing student in a sterile gown accidentally lets their hands drop below their waist. What should they do?

options.A: Step back one foot and continue assisting the surgeon
options.B: Continue working because the gown is still clean on top
options.C: Acknowledge that sterility is broken and get a new gown
options.D: Ask the circulating nurse to wipe the gloves with alcohol

explanation: In theatre rules, anything below the waist is considered unsterile. Don't worry—accidents happen! Just step back, re-gown, and keep learning. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T13#GNS123_U5_T13_h7)

question: Why is a pregnant teenager at a much higher risk for nutritional shortages than an adult pregnant woman?

options.A: She is still growing herself and must compete with the fetus for nutrients.
options.B: Adult women require half the daily calories of teenagers.
options.C: Her digestive tract is shorter and absorbs fewer vitamins overall.
options.D: Hormones during teen pregnancy completely block fat digestion.

explanation: Correct! The teen's body is still finishing its own growth spurt while also feeding a growing baby, creating a huge demand for extra nutrients. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T6#GNS312_U3_T6_h7)

question: What is the ultimate goal of patient education when teaching someone how to care for their diabetes at home?

options.A: Preventing the patient from ever experiencing normal life stress
options.B: Eliminating all future visits to the primary healthcare clinic
options.C: Empowering the patient to safely manage their daily condition
options.D: Ensuring the family takes complete control of medication administration

explanation: Good education gives patients the tools, knowledge, and confidence to take charge of their own health every day. Love to see it! [learn more](GNS324_U4_T17#GNS324_U4_T17_h8)

question: A staff nurse administers the wrong IV fluid, injuring a patient while on duty in a public hospital. Who can be sued alongside the nurse?

options.A: The patient's next of kin
options.B: The hospital management or employing authority
options.C: The Nursing and Midwifery Council registrar
options.D: The pharmaceutical manufacturing company

explanation: Because the nurse was doing their job at the time, the hospital shares the responsibility under the rule of vicarious liability. Teamwork means shared accountability! [learn more](GST321_U10_T4#GST321_U10_T4_h5)

question: How do the internal and external urethral sphincters differ from each other?

options.A: The internal sphincter is smooth muscle while the external sphincter is skeletal muscle.
options.B: The internal sphincter is voluntary while the external sphincter is entirely involuntary.
options.C: Both sphincters are made entirely of involuntary smooth muscle.
options.D: Both sphincters are made exclusively of skeletal muscle fibers.

explanation: Think of it this way: the internal sphincter works automatically (smooth muscle), while the external one is under your conscious control so you can hold it (skeletal muscle). Great job! [learn more](GNS121_U2_T9#GNS121_U2_T9_h1)

question: What is the main nursing priority right after delivery for a patient who had placenta accreta?

options.A: Monitoring for signs of postpartum hemorrhage and shock
options.B: Administering oral iron supplements for mild fatigue
options.C: Encouraging immediate ambulation around the ward
options.D: Preparing the infant for immediate nursery discharge

explanation: Because accreta makes it hard for the uterus to contract properly and clear all tissue, keeping a close eye on bleeding is your number one lifesaving duty. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T6#GNS121_U6_T6_h8)

question: What is the main difference between 'change' and 'transition' in a hospital setting?

options.A: Change only affects doctors, while transition only affects bedside nurses.
options.B: Change happens slowly over years, whereas transition happens instantly.
options.C: Change is an external event, while transition is the internal emotional process.
options.D: Change is psychological, while transition is purely structural.

explanation: Brilliant distinction! Change is the physical new policy or machine, while transition is how our minds and hearts catch up to it. [learn more](GST319_U2_T5#GST319_U2_T5_h4)

question: Under most Nigerian laws, what is the main legal exception that allows for an abortion?

options.A: If the family cannot afford a child
options.B: When requested by the husband
options.C: If the pregnancy occurs during school term
options.D: To save the life of the pregnant woman

explanation: Nigerian law is very strict regarding abortion, but saving the mother's life is recognized as a legal exception. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h5)

question: Which lifestyle change makes the biggest difference in preventing oral cancer?

options.A: Avoiding all dairy products in the diet
options.B: Taking daily multivitamin supplements
options.C: Using hard-bristled toothbrushes twice daily
options.D: Stopping tobacco use and limiting alcohol

explanation: Smoking, tobacco use, and heavy drinking are the main culprits behind most oral cancers. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T4#GNS213_U3_T4_h7)

question: What common mental health challenge can block an older adult's progress during physical rehabilitation?

options.A: Euphoria
options.B: Depression
options.C: Hyperactivity
options.D: Megalomania

explanation: You're doing great! Depression drains a patient's drive and energy, making it tough for them to participate in rehab exercises. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T6#GNS321_U3_T6_h5)

question: What is the main reason for doing a pelvic ultrasound when post-abortion complications are suspected?

options.A: To determine the patient's exact psychological state
options.B: To check for retained products of conception or free fluid
options.C: To test for specific bacterial strains causing infection
options.D: To measure the patient's exact blood clotting time

explanation: An ultrasound gives doctors a clear 'window' inside to check if any pregnancy tissue was left behind or if fluid leaked where it shouldn't. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T009#GNS226_U5_T009_h6)

question: What does the principle of autonomy mean in family planning?

options.A: Clinics must provide free medications to every community member
options.B: Husbands must approve all medical treatments before they begin
options.C: Clients have the right to make their own choices without coercion
options.D: Nurses must choose the safest contraceptive for young clients

explanation: Autonomy protects the client's right to self-determination in their personal reproductive healthcare decisions. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h2)

question: What does it mean when a Drug Revolving Fund is described as 'ring-fenced'?

options.A: The pharmacy door must be locked with a special metal ring
options.B: Drugs are arranged in circular shelves inside the store
options.C: Profits are shared equally among all clinical department heads
options.D: Money from drug sales is kept separate and used only to buy more drugs

explanation: Ring-fencing is like putting a protective fence around the money. It ensures drug funds aren't mistakenly used to pay for other hospital bills! [learn more](GNS215_U3_T7#GNS215_U3_T7_h3)

question: What is the primary function of plasmin during the healing process?

options.A: It breaks down and dissolves the fibrin clot
options.B: It stimulates the rapid production of new platelets
options.C: It causes the initial vascular spasm in injured vessels

options.C: The infant is safe because colic is a temporary developmental stage

explanation: Young age, mental stress, money troubles, and a fussy baby pile up to create high risk. This family needs extra support! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T24#GNS225_U5_T24_h3)

question: What is the key difference between monitoring and evaluating an IEC campaign?

options.A: Monitoring is done by doctors, while evaluation is done exclusively by government auditors.
options.B: Monitoring happens after the campaign ends, while evaluation happens before printing.
options.C: Monitoring tracks distribution activities, while evaluation measures actual health outcomes and behavior changes.
options.D: Monitoring looks at money spent, while evaluation looks at paper quality.

explanation: Think of monitoring as tracking your daily steps during the campaign, while evaluation checks the final results and lifestyle changes at the end. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T6#GNS124_U5_T6_h6)

question: Your patient just came back from abdominal surgery. Their tummy feels a bit swollen and you can't hear any bowel sounds. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Administer a strong laxative orally right away
options.B: Massage the abdomen vigorously to force gas out
options.C: Encourage the patient to eat a large solid meal
options.D: Keep the patient NPO until bowel activity returns

explanation: If the bowel isn't moving (paralytic ileus), giving food or drink will only cause nausea and vomiting. Keeping them NPO (nothing by mouth) keeps them safe until peristalsis wakes up! [learn more](GNS121_U1_T4#GNS121_U1_T4_h8)

question: A grateful family tries to give you an expensive cash gift for your home care. What is the right response?

options.A: Accept the gift privately to avoid hurting the family's feelings
options.B: Divide the money evenly among all members of the healthcare team
options.C: Keep the money as a bonus for providing excellent home care
options.D: Politely decline the gift while explaining professional boundary policies

explanation: It's a kind gesture from the family, but accepting expensive gifts compromises your professional objectivity. Always decline with kindness and grace. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T23#GNS225_U2_T23_h8)

question: Why do we love using the metric system in healthcare?

options.A: Only international companies use it
options.B: It means no math is ever needed
options.C: Patients never ask questions about it
options.D: It uses a simple base-ten scale that makes conversions safe and easy

explanation: Base-ten means you can convert units just by moving the decimal point. No complicated math required! [learn more](GNS122_U1_T23#GNS122_U1_T23_h3)

question: What is the gold-standard test to confirm a patient truly has gout?

options.A: Performing a standard chest X-ray on the patient
options.B: Measuring the daily protein intake in the diet
options.C: Checking a routine blood pressure reading in the clinic
options.D: Examining joint fluid under a microscope for crystals

explanation: You got it! Drawing a little fluid out of the angry joint and spotting those sneaky uric acid crystals under a microscope gives a 100% definite diagnosis. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T16#GNS222_U1_T16_h5)

question: A patient is in the ICU after having a heart myxoma removed. What is a top nursing priority?

options.A: Encouraging heavy weightlifting to rebuild chest muscle strength
options.B: Restricting all fluid intake to zero for the first week
options.C: Monitoring continuous cardiac telemetry and vital signs
options.D: Removing the chest tubes without provider orders

explanation: After heart surgery, keeping a close eye on the heart rhythm and vital signs lets you spot and tackle complications right away. You are thinking like a real ICU nurse! [learn more](GNS213_U1_T8#GNS213_U1_T8_h7)

question: What is the main reason nurses send a sample to the lab for a microbial culture?

options.A: To measure the exact number of red blood cells in circulation
options.B: To detect circulating antibodies produced by the patient's immune system
options.C: To grow and identify the specific microorganism causing the infection
options.D: To visualize stained tissue sections under a high-powered microscope

explanation: A culture gives germs a cozy place to multiply so the lab can figure out exactly what bug is making your patient sick. [learn more](GST114_U3_T2#GST114_U3_T2_h4)

question: A nurse is feeling burnt out after seeing multiple emergency cases. Which type of support is best?

options.A: Formative supervision
options.B: Restorative supervision
options.C: Administrative supervision
options.D: Normative supervision

explanation: When clinical work drains you emotionally, restorative supervision steps in to restore your peace of mind and help you cope with stress. [learn more](GST321_U1_T17#GST321_U1_T17_h3)

question: Why did people in early history practice family planning?

options.A: To increase the speed of urban industrial growth
options.B: To comply with modern hospital guidelines
options.C: To eliminate the need for traditional birth attendants
options.D: To manage family size and resource allocation

explanation: Even long ago, communities needed to make sure they had enough food and resources for everyone, so they practiced family planning to manage family size. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T001#GNS226_U6_T001_h1)

question: What is the main way hormonal contraceptives work in the body?

options.A: To speed up the fertilization process in the fallopian tubes
options.B: To mimic natural feedback loops and halt the release of eggs
options.C: To permanently destroy the reproductive organs of a patient
options.D: To increase the natural production of estrogen in the ovaries

explanation: You've got this! Hormonal contraceptives use synthetic hormones to gently trick the body's natural feedback system so that ovulation (releasing an egg) doesn't happen. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T17#GNS215_U6_T17_h1)

question: At what CD4+ cell count is an HIV infection typically classified as AIDS?

options.A: Below 500 cells per microliter
options.B: Below 1000 cells per microliter
options.C: Below 1500 cells per microliter
options.D: Below 200 cells per microliter

explanation: When the CD4 count drops below 200 cells per microliter, it shows severe immune weakness and meets the clinical definition of AIDS. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T13#GNS216_U6_T13_h1)

question: What is the best way for a nursing team to share their successful hospital study with others?

options.A: Keeping the final report locked inside a private desk drawer
options.B: Presenting at a healthcare conference or publishing in a peer-reviewed journal
options.C: Posting raw data sheets on a public community notice board
options.D: Destroying all copies to protect hospital operational secrets

explanation: Good nursing knowledge is meant to be shared! Conferences and journals help spread great ideas so patient care improves everywhere. [learn more](GNS224_U3_T3#GNS224_U3_T3_h8)
